raw_response:
I’m 54 this year, and I’ve farmed these fields a long time. I don’t read many technical things, so I mostly judge by what I saw on my own land and what the capable farmers in the village did. This year I still won’t push too hard. Cotton is still my main crop because I know how to manage it, and with some family working off-farm I can’t put all 64 mu into crops that need too much hand labor at the same time. I’ll keep some land in wheat-maize because that gives steadier grain income and spreads the risk. I’ll keep a small piece of stevia because a few neighbors said it still sells if you manage it carefully, but I won’t expand it too much because the market can change and it needs attention.

For cotton, I’ll put most of the land there, about 36 mu. Cotton has been my habit for years, and with well water I can hold it if the weather turns dry. I’ll use the kind of seed people nearby are planting, not the most expensive one, and I’ll put enough fertilizer so the crop doesn’t look weak later. I won’t save too much on fertilizer, because if cotton sits there thin all season, I lose more than I save. But I also won’t pour money into it like a big farm. For wheat and maize, I’ll keep 20 mu in double cropping on the same land. Wheat gives me something steady, then maize goes in right after harvest, same as everybody here. The turn is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and hire machinery when needed. For stevia, I’ll leave 8 mu. That’s enough to try for cash income without tying up too much money or labor. This year my idea is simple: steady crops on most land, a little cash crop, and don’t spend so much at the start that I have no cash left if water, pests, or family needs come up.
